tb21_profile.skill: Build a large third-party source tree end to end: satisfy the toolchain and library prerequisites, run ./configure with the correct host OS/ISA target, drive make through its failures, and leave a working binary at an exact path
tb21_profile.domain: Unix source builds — autoconf/configure, make, cross/host target triples, compiler and language toolchains (here OCaml/Coq)
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging: compile-a-named-version-from-source until the produced artifact runs

searches: tools.py search tmax 'no internet|offline|without network access|air-gapped' -n 25
tools.py search all 'LLVM|llvm|build (gcc|clang|the compiler)|verified compiler|CompCert|formal verification' -n 30
tools.py search rts 'build .{0,25}from source|compile .{0,25}from source|\./configure|make install|cross-compilation|toolchain' -n 40
sqlite: SELECT task_id FROM doc WHERE source='SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean' AND task_id LIKE '%conan%'/'%tox%'/'%cookiecutter%'/'%pip%'
sqlite: SELECT task_id FROM doc WHERE source='SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean' AND task_id LIKE '%setuptools%'/'%cibuildwheel%'/'%scikit%'/'%nox%'/'%pip-%'/'%pipx%'/'%conan%'

TMax-15K.reason: Repair a broken offline zlib-1.3 source tree, build it, then build the dependent tool against it; no-network dependency build.
Fix a deliberately broken build configuration in a vendored SQLite source tree and compile it into a working artifact.
Fix and install a vendored simdjson v3.6.0 source drop, then build the consumer against it; exact-version source build.
make on the vendored wrk source fails on a missing dependency; diagnose, satisfy it, build and run the tool.
Find the Makefile perturbation in vendored xxHash-0.8.2, build libxxhash.a and statically link it into a new binary.
Build against a vendored zlib-1.3.1 whose configuration is wrong; library-plus-consumer build chain repair.
Repair the vendored SQLite build script so the amalgamation compiles, then use the result downstream.
Build a C++ tool on top of a vendored simdjson v3.6.0 tree; compiler flags and include/link wiring are the work.
With no internet, fix the local nlohmann/json header so the project compiles; offline dependency repair.
Vendored pen-0.34.1 C source must be corrected and rebuilt into a working load balancer binary.

Download PostgreSQL 16.2 source, configure, build and install under a named prefix; exact-version source build ending in a runnable binary.
Same PostgreSQL 16.2 tarball-to-installed-prefix build, different framing; configure/make/make install discipline.
Build and system-wide-install Paho MQTT Embedded-C from source, then compile a client against the installed headers and libs.
Third PostgreSQL 16.2 from-source variant; same configure-build-install-to-prefix skill on a large C codebase.
Compile Fennel 0.4.1 to WebAssembly with Emscripten; building a language implementation for a specific target with a non-default toolchain.
Install an MT2735 cross-compiler toolchain from an archive, verify it against its manifest and report; toolchain provisioning.
Same cross toolchain plus the aarch64-poky-linux sysroot extraction and a reconciled installation report.
Build docker-lvm-plugin from source including its man page and install it system-wide; Makefile-driven build and install.
Multi-file C build that must use a compiler version the spec pins, then reconcile the produced artifacts; toolchain-version matching.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Configure and build binutils 2.27 as an LFS cross-toolchain targeting $LFS_TGT; configure-for-the-right-target is the crux, as with CompCert.
Compile Python 3.9.1 from source on Debian and end with a working python3.9 executable; same version-pinned build-and-prove-it-runs.
Build MBDyn 1.7.3 from source and then actually simulate a model with it; build plus functional verification of the produced binary.
Build VIM from source with a specific feature set and interpreter bindings and install to an exact path; configure-flag selection drives everything.
Clone, prepare prerequisites and autotools-build Singularity so the binary is on PATH system-wide.
Build Git from source, resolving its build prerequisites, and leave a working install.
Configure the build with the i586-elf- cross-compiler prefix and compile the OS; picking the right target toolchain prefix is the whole difficulty.
Compile Julia from source after pulling upstream; a long, dependency-heavy build that has to actually finish.
Build Neovim from source in a prepared checkout; straightforward but the same make-it-actually-build genre.
Configure and build Ruby 2.6 from source with substituted compiler wrappers; forces care about which CC/CXX the build picks up.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: GNU triplet generation broken for mips/mips64/s390; mapping an architecture to the right build triple is exactly CompCert's configure step.
Wrong C++ standard flags emitted per Clang/GCC version; compiler-version-dependent flag selection, the usual source-build failure mode.
GnuDepsFlags applies Apple framework flags on non-Apple OSes; OS-conditional build flags, the other half of configure detection.
Incorrect C++ standard flags for Clang across versions; same compiler-capability-to-flag mapping problem.
CMakeDeps mishandles transitive dependencies; getting a dependency chain to link is the recurring cost of building from source.
Profile subsettings not invalidated when the compiler setting changes; reasoning about a build profile's consistency.
Profile.dumps drops the settings section; serialising the os/arch/compiler configuration a build depends on.
BazelDeps component name resolution wrong; generating correct build-system inputs for a dependency graph.
Dependency-graph filtering is wrong; reasoning about a package dependency tree, which is what stalls source builds.
Hook subprocess failures are swallowed and misreported; correctly surfacing a failing build step's error.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Wheel ABI tag computed wrong for a debug Python build; detecting the host interpreter/ABI correctly is the configure-detection problem.
CIBW_ENVIRONMENT no longer reaches the compile step; getting build-time environment variables to the compiler, a classic configure failure.
CMake-backed build backend crashes on boolean config settings; passing build options through to the native build system.
Building a package whose sources sit in a subdirectory; invoking the build in the right working tree, as CompCert requires.
pip-sync picks the first pip on PATH instead of the matching interpreter's; picking the right toolchain binary out of several.
Transitive setup_requires must override system versions; build-time dependency resolution against what is already installed.
build_meta omits setup.py from the sdist, so a from-source build of the package fails downstream.
Install via 'python -m pip' rather than the bare 'pip' binary; same class of which-tool-am-I-actually-running bug.
Git remote parsing fails on treeless clones during source acquisition; fetching the sources a build needs.
setup.cfg metadata does not honour setup_requires; declarative build configuration not taking effect.

final_top10.reason: Build Janus v0.10.5 and three pinned dependencies from source, verify tarball checksums, install to a fixed prefix. Same shape as CompCert 3.13.1.
Fetch, configure, build and install PostgreSQL 16.2 under a named prefix; exact-version source build ending in a usable binary.
Compile Python 3.9.1 from source and prove the produced executable runs; version-pinned build with a working-binary acceptance test.
Configure binutils 2.27 for a specific target triple and build it; choosing the right configure target is CompCert's central step.
Build MBDyn 1.7.3 from source then run a model through it; build plus a functional check of the artifact, like invoking ./ccomp.
Configure VIM with a demanding feature/interpreter set and install to an exact path; configure-flag selection against available libraries.
Second PostgreSQL 16.2 tarball-to-prefix build; reinforces configure/make/make install on a large C tree.
Install build prerequisites and autotools-build Singularity from a git checkout until the binary is on PATH.
Build and install a C library from source, then compile and run a client against the installed artifact; end-to-end usability check.
Configure the build with the correct cross-compiler prefix before compiling; target/toolchain selection is the failure point.

notes: No corpus contains an OCaml/Coq/opam build (4 OCaml hits pool-wide, all trivial QCheck tasks), so nobody scores 5 on the exact ecosystem. TerminalWorld and RTS are the right pools here and both were under-ranked by the lexical retrievers: RTS's PostgreSQL-16.2-from-source and Janus-v0.10.5-from-source clusters were absent from the shortlist entirely and I found them with a 'build from source | ./configure | make install' regex. I deliberately ranked TMax below them: TMax's 1200+ build tasks are almost all 'find the deliberate perturbation in a Makefile', which is a find-the-bug genre rather than a provision-and-configure-a-real-build genre, so they score well on domain and poorly on task_form. For the two SWE corpora I judged on domain and scored the conan cluster (GNU triplets, per-compiler flags, OS-conditional flags, CMakeDeps) highest, because that is the same target-triple and toolchain-flag reasoning ./configure does; setuptools/cibuildwheel cover host-ABI detection and build-environment propagation.
